Burned up
bernd áp
Very angry — Furioso/a / quemado/a.
He was really burned up about the decision.
Informal. From burn up, meaning to make someone angry.
Do with
du uith
Would like or need something — Venirle bien / necesitar.
I could do with a coffee.
v|Only in could do with or can do with. Not the same as do without.
Get off on
guet óf ón
Enjoy something a great deal — Disfrutar con / ponerle a uno.
He gets off on winning arguments.
v|Not separable. Informal, and can sound crude.
Go with
góu uith
Be usually found together — Ir con / acompañar a.
A lot of responsibility goes with that job.
Look good together — Combinar con / pegar con.
That blouse goes with your skirt.
Choose something from the options — Decantarse por / quedarse con.
I think I'll go with the black one.
v|Not separable. Irregular: goes with, went with, gone with.
Piss off
pis óf
Make someone very angry — Cabrear / fastidiar.
It really pissed him off.
v|Separable. Rude in every sense; say annoy or irritate unless you know the company well.
Put past
put past
Believe someone capable of something bad — Ver capaz de.
I wouldn't put it past him to lie.
v|Only in the negative: I wouldn't put it past someone.
